summary.text: Craig Williams is a Republican member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from District 160, having taken office on December 1, 2020, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A retired Marine Corps colonel, his career includes work as a federal prosecutor.

paragraphs.text: Williams lives in Concord Township, Pennsylvania, and served in the United States Marine Corps for 28 years, reaching the rank of colonel.
He graduated from Bartlett High School in 1983, earned a B.A. from Duke University in 1987, a J.D. from the University of Florida in 1997, and an LL.M. from Columbia University School of Law in 2001.
His career experience includes working as deputy legal counsel to the chair of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and as a federal prosecutor with the U.S. Department of Justice.

In the 2023-2024 session, Williams was assigned to the Consumer Protection & Professional Licensure, Human Services, and Veterans Affairs & Emergency Preparedness committees, serving as a subcommittee chair on each.
